title: Media and data — Table, Chart, Icon, Image
status: ACCEPTED — all four components rendered in a real DSH host, both schemes measured, security policy exercised
verdict: ACCEPTED. All six exit-gate items have evidence on this machine. The batch's distinguishing risk was not rendering but two security questions, both decided in ADRs before the renderers existed: ADR-009 (an Image may load only an absolute http/https URL) and ADR-010 (a Chart is a structured row contract rendered as countable SVG, never a Chart.js clone).

decisions.title: The Image component's source policy
decisions.summary: An Image renders a real only for an absolute http: or https: URL, parsed with new URL and never pattern-matched. data:, blob:, file:, javascript:, protocol-relative and relative sources render the alt text in a bordered placeholder naming the reason. Workspace paths are deliberately unsupported here: the node-side reader in src/images.ts needs an execute step and a sandboxed frame that this backend does not have, because the OpenUI card is mounted in the host document.

decisions.title: The Chart parameter contract
decisions.summary: data is an array of row objects, x names the category key and series the value keys. Invalid data draws a stated refusal rather than a blank or a coerced zero; a non-finite value is a gap and is counted in a notice. SVG rather than Canvas so every bar and slice is countable in a test and in the host DOM. No options object, no animation, no tooltips — recorded as out of scope so a later batch adds them as a decision.

securityEvidence.claim: A refused scheme produces no element at all, in the host document
securityEvidence.unit: tests/openui-media-4a4.spec.tsx — javascript:, data:, file:, blob:, //host/x, relative, rooted and empty all assert countOf(html, 'img') === 0
securityEvidence.browser: C1-four-components.json — measured.image.imgs === 1, and every src starts with https:
securityEvidence.whyItMatters: The OpenUI card is mounted in the host document, not the HTML backend's sandboxed iframe, so a javascript: src would be a host-origin question.
securityEvidence.mutation: M1: making allowedImageUrl accept every scheme turned two tests red (the refused-scheme test and the reason test), then restored.

securityEvidence.claim: The refusal names the reason and does not echo the hostile payload
securityEvidence.browser: The refusal reads 'javascript: is not an allowed scheme (http or https only)' — the scheme is named, the alert(1) payload is not re-inserted into the DOM

mutationChecks.purpose: a guard that has never been seen to go red is a guess about what it protects
mutationChecks.M1: allowedImageUrl accepts every scheme -> 'produces NO element for any refused scheme' and 'names the reason' both fail
mutationChecks.M2: chartSeries coerces an unreadable value to 0 -> 'refuses when no numeric series can be found' and 'treats a non-finite value as a gap' both fail
mutationChecks.M3: Table draws only the cells that exist -> 'pads a short row rather than shifting the cells' fails
mutationChecks.O1: validate gate replaced with a stub returning no errors -> 'rejects Action([...])' and 'rejects an unknown @-function' both fail
mutationChecks.note: All four mutations were restored and the suites re-run green.

observations.summary: The unit spec bypassed the backend's name check — CLOSED in this batch
observations.detail: recorded in 4A-3 as a test-fidelity gap. tests/openui-validate-gate.spec.ts now runs fixtures through openuiBackend().validate(), the same entry the tool path uses, so a fixture the host would refuse fails in the suite. It asserts both directions: the documented bare @Set form is accepted, and Action([...]) is rejected with VZO002 — the shape the live host refuses.
observations.status: Fixed. Proven to go red by replacing the error list with a stub.

defects.summary: Table used 'raw' without declaring it, and the new spec was missing both the jsdom pragma and its tsconfig registration
defects.detail: The renderer signature had to grow a fourth parameter; the spec needed // @vitest-environment jsdom to reach document, and then had to be excluded from the node project and included in the client project like every other .tsx spec. Typecheck caught all three.
defects.status: Fixed. Recorded because the tsconfig pair is a step a new batch will have to repeat.

openQuestions.topic: A remote Image URL is still fetched by the reader's browser
openQuestions.detail: ADR-009 closes the scheme set but cannot prevent a request to an attacker-chosen https host. That is inherent to an in a host document.
openQuestions.whyRecorded: so a later move to node-side resolution is a decision that cites ADR-009 and adds the isPublicAddress check images.ts already has, rather than a silent regression
